newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ ELECTION - Party policies on superannuation.
newsitem.headline: NZ ELECTION - Party policies on superannuation.

text.p: Here is a summary of how the main parties contesting New Zealand's general election on Saturday stand on superannuation.
NATIONAL
* The National government has raised the superannuation surtax threshold with effect from April 1, 1997 to $297 a week of other income for couples and to $198 for single superannuitants.
* Signatory to multi-party accord which puts a base of 65 percent of average after-tax wage for couples.
* Not advocating further changes.
* Retain asset testing for long stay geriatric care.
LABOUR
* Abolish the surtax and asset testing for geriatric care.
* Provide a one-off five percent increase in the pension over and above the regular inflation adjustment.
* Dedicate eight percent of income tax to an independently managed super fund.
* Signatory to multi-party accord.
NEW ZEALAND FIRST
* Only main party not signatory to the accord.
* Would abolish the surtax.
* Inflation-adjust super payments every six months
* Introduce a compulsory savings scheme with contributions beginning at three percent of all income above $5000, and rising to eight percent by 2003.
* A choice of private schemes and a public scheme with guaranteed rates of return. Income would be in addition to state-funded pension, which would continue.
* Free public hospital geriatric care
* Remove asset but not income testing for long-stay private or public geriatric hospital care.
* Family home exempt from asset testing for private rest-home care.
* State-run home equity scheme to allow superannuitants to borrow up to 20 percent of value of home for personal use. $150 million available for this.
ALLIANCE
* Signatory to accord.
* Abolish superannuation surcharge and raise super payments to 72.5 percent of average after-tax wage.
* Abolish income and asset testing for longstay geriatric care.
* Pay a senior citizens benefit equal to 95 percent of superannuation to people aged 60-65.
UNITED
* Persuaded National to set up the Taskforce on Positive Ageing, and is awaiting its recommendations.
* Insisted asset testing be included in the taskforce's brief.
* Was instrumental in getting surtax thresholds raised.
ACT
* Abolish superannuation surcharge.

* Compulsory savings scheme: seven percent of individual's income would be invested with private superannuation fund of own choice, until $155,000 in today's dollars accumulated. State would top up savings of those without time or income to accumulate $155,000. Fund available only at age 65.
* Existing superannuitants and soon-to-retire would continue to receive state support.
CHRISTIAN COALITION
* Abolish super surcharge and asset testing for geriatric hospital patients.
* Move to a personal contributory pension scheme, providing tax incentives for saving.
-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
